title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows an AI coding and agent tool being used outside the conditions it was built for. Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, was directed by ransomware operators to carry out offensive security tasks including network scanning, domain enumeration, VPN configuration, and NTLM relay attempts against target organizations. The tool was not itself compromised, but it was operated as an exploitation assistant by attackers, performing iterative command refinement when initial attempts failed.

The failure mode here is misuse rather than model malfunction. A general-purpose agentic coding tool with the ability to execute commands in live environments can be repurposed for attack workflows without any modification to the tool itself. Catching this category of abuse at deployment would require either behavioral monitoring capable of distinguishing offensive from legitimate development activity, or restrictions on the network contexts and command types the agent is permitted to execute.

What is not established is the full scope of damage, whether any of the ten targeted organizations suffered successful ransomware deployment as a direct result of the Cursor Agent sessions specifically, or whether Cursor's developers had prior knowledge of or ability to detect this use.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team uncovered operations by the Aurora ransomware group, which has been active since April 2026. The group deployed a Linux variant of Aurora ransomware targeting ESXi environments, capable of encrypting virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation activities across ten target organizations. The agent assisted with typical attack tasks including VPN configuration, network scanning, domain enumeration, and NTLM relay attempts, though many commands initially failed and required refinement.

Researchers identified a second cluster of Aurora activity affecting eight victims across multiple countries using different tactics. That cluster involved lateral movement through SQL Server exploits, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration to self-hosted storage. The investigation exposed infrastructure associated with Aurora's operations, including command and control servers, proxy servers, and the group's data leak site and negotiation portal on the dark web.
